chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Rock takes over the Canadian club
summary: Jazz rooms turn to rock; the Colonial Inn, where his band had packed the place, brings in flashing lights and go-go girls.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Finally, I just had to move back. And, so, this is what I'm talking about - when anyone asks you - how did you survive -- those years and then, of course, you know Rock was big and coming in strong as hell, you know, and it was just putting a lot of guys-- a lot of jazz places in America were turning to Rock - changing their policy completely. Like the place in Canada. Now, we played in Canada; we used to go up there and play - eight weeks and come back quickly for four more and such and one time in one year, we worked five times in the same place; they just kept wanting us back because we were packing the joint out and the waiters were so happy when they saw our band because they made all the tips and things while we were there. That was the Colonial Inn -- the Colonial Inn today is practically a strip joint---

And, then, it went to Rock and once I went in there while they were having Rock and we started to play and suddenly all the lights started to flash on and I said to the guy -"what the hell is that?" Because that's what the Rock guys use - all the flashing lights and--- and I said --"my band can't play with that going on - what the hell is that?" So, they turned off all the fancy lights, you know. But, you see, they were well on their way to Rock; they had--
---fixed the whole place up to play for Rock - to do Rock. And, now, it's a nothing - you
see - they went that policy, they have little go go girls there---
